fish.name: Pebbleskip Dace
fish.flavor: Skims across the shallows in three neat bounces, exactly like a thrown pebble. Local children insist they invented it.

fish.name: Bridgetoll Minnow
fish.flavor: Loiters under the old bridge demanding a toll of one breadcrumb. Nobody has ever paid, and yet it persists, generation after generation.

fish.name: Riffle Whistler
fish.flavor: Whistles through the rapids at a pitch only kettles and grandmothers can hear. Both find it deeply reassuring.

fish.name: Eddy Loach
fish.flavor: Has spent its entire life going in one slow circle behind the same rock. It considers this a career.

fish.name: Backchat Bleak
fish.flavor: Whatever you shout under the bridge, it mouths back a beat later, slightly wrong and somehow ruder.

fish.name: Laundry-Day Roach
fish.flavor: Turns up wherever washing is done in the river, chewing thoughtfully on a sleeve. Returns nothing, apologizes for nothing.

fish.name: Clockwise Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Only turns clockwise, ever, on anything. Going left requires two hundred and seventy degrees of quiet commitment.

fish.name: Wobbly Chub
fish.flavor: Swims like it is remembering how in real time. The current forgives it; the current forgives everyone.

fish.name: Millwheel Shiner
fish.flavor: Rides the old waterwheel up, glitters at the top, and plunges back down. It has done this eleven thousand times and gasps every single time.

fish.name: Contrary Grayling
fish.flavor: Swims upstream exclusively, on principle. Nobody remembers what the principle is, least of all the grayling.

fish.name: Stepping-Stone Sculpin
fish.flavor: Flat, grey, and perfectly stone-shaped. If a stepping stone has ever lurched beneath you mid-crossing, apologies: that was probably this.

fish.name: Miller's Thumbling
fish.flavor: Broad-headed, like an old miller's flattened thumb. The mill closed a century ago, but the thumblings still keep its hours.

fish.name: Ticklish Trout
fish.flavor: Trout-ticklers swear it giggles. The trout swears it was a cough. The dispute is ongoing.

fish.name: Drizzle Darter
fish.flavor: Only bites when it is raining just enough to be annoying. The village meteorologist has started consulting it.

fish.name: Hobnail Bullhead
fish.flavor: Studded down the back like a workman's boot, and clomps against the riverbed loudly enough to wake the mayflies. They do not thank it.

fish.name: Fingerling Fib
fish.flavor: The fish that got away, before it gets away. Measures four inches; will be remembered as twelve.

fish.name: Knotwork Eel
fish.flavor: Ties itself into old borderland knots when nervous, which is always. Untangling one counts as either fishing or archaeology.

fish.name: Troll's Whisker
fish.flavor: Long, bristly, and found only beneath the oldest bridges. If it is what its name suggests, it is best not to think about the size of the chin.

fish.name: Widdershins Pike
fish.flavor: Circles you counterclockwise before striking, which the old folk say invites misfortune. The pike says it simply likes the approach angle.

fish.name: Rainstitch Trout
fish.flavor: Its speckles line up like stitches, as if someone sewed it together out of rain and never quite tied off the thread.

fish.name: Fiddler's Bream
fish.flavor: Rises whenever someone plays a fiddle on the bridge. It has strong opinions about tempo and expresses them by splashing.

fish.name: Foxfire Loach
fish.flavor: Carries a faint rotten-log glow it very obviously stole from somewhere. The forest has not asked for it back, yet.

fish.name: Weary Kelt
fish.flavor: Went up the river, spawned, came all the way back down, and has been sighing about it ever since. Take it home; it needs the rest.

fish.name: Nixie's Comb
fish.flavor: Slim as a comb's spine, with fins like teeth. The nixies miss it terribly, or so the drowned-sounding singing suggests.

fish.name: Bottlepost Minnow
fish.flavor: Swallows messages in bottles and delivers them, eventually, to precisely the wrong person. Half the village's feuds and both of its marriages are its doing.

fish.name: Déjà Dace
fish.flavor: You have caught this exact fish before. You are sure of it. It regards you with the same suspicion.

fish.name: Kelpie's Bridle
fish.flavor: Cold to the touch, jingles faintly, and pulls toward deep water when held. Whatever it was buckled to is still out there, unbridled.

fish.name: Greenteeth Grinner
fish.flavor: Grins up from the weeds with too many green teeth. Grandmothers warn children off the riverbank; the grinner does it far more efficiently.

fish.name: The Understudy
fish.flavor: Takes the shape of the last fish you caught, but nervously, like it is not quite off-book yet. Applaud when you release it; it needs this.

fish.name: Yesterday's Salmon
fish.flavor: Arrives a day before it swims past, and leaves a week before that. Catch it today; you already did.

fish.name: Rushlight Gar
fish.flavor: Burns down its own spine like a rushlight in a cottage window. Nobody knows what it keeps vigil for, but it has not gone out in living memory.

fish.name: Stone-Sleeper
fish.flavor: The oldest masonry in the second bridge arch is not masonry. Once a decade it wakes to yawn, and the whole bridge groans with it.

fish.name: Undertow Chorister
fish.flavor: Sings one low note in the dark pull beneath the rapids. Fishers who hum along report a strange calm and, occasionally, missing hats.

fish.name: The Toll Collector
fish.flavor: Beneath the first bridge ever built over this river sits something that took coin before there was coin. Every fish caught upstream has paid it a scale in passing, and yours is due.

fish.name: The Rapids' Grin
fish.flavor: On white-water days the rapids show teeth, and it is not the water. It has never harmed a soul, which somehow makes the grin worse.

fish.name: Naiad's Needle
fish.flavor: A sliver of living silver said to stitch the current back together after storms tear it. Look closely at any seam in the river: the stitches are even.

fish.name: The Second Reflection
fish.flavor: Beneath your reflection there is another, and it does not always do what you do. On calm evenings, it fishes for you.

fish.name: The Salmon of Somewhen
fish.flavor: It has already been caught by everyone who will ever catch it, and remembers each of you fondly. Ask your question quickly; you only get the answer you were always going to get.

fish.name: The River's First Name
fish.flavor: Before the mapmakers came, the river chose a name for itself, and it lives in this fish's mouth. Those who hear it spoken can only describe the sound afterwards as: home.

fish.name: The Long Silver
fish.flavor: The oldest maps do not mark a river through these hills; they mark a fish. Everything you have ever caught was swimming in its wake.
